subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm deciding this vehicle can be a static model without joints since it's not a creature rig, with parts attached directly under the root. I'm sketching the design as an armoured hauler truck with six wheels, a forward cab, a flatbed with a sealed glowing cargo pod, armor plating, and neon accent strips.

I'm planning out the scale (roughly 8m long, 3.5m tall) and reviewing how to use the builder's part, paint, and glow kit APIs for geometry, rotation, and surface texturing, then starting to lay out the chassis frame and wheel positions along the Z axis.

Now I'm placing three axles of wheels with their radius, width, hub glow details, and fenders, then building the cab with a boxy body and an extruded sloped windshield profile.

I'm working out the windshield's placement and tilt as a thin rotated box, calculating its center position, length, and the rotation angle needed so its normal faces forward-up along the slope direction.

Offsetting the windshield plane slightly outward along its normal for correct placement. For side windows, I'm positioning textured planes on the cab's left and right faces matching the body width and window opening height. I'm also planning a front bumper box with dark coloring and possibly diagonal hazard stripe texture, plus considering a front plow/ram plate wedge shape extending forward.

I'll build the plow as a narrowing frustum box extending from the cab front outward, then add glowing headlight boxes near the top of the front face, magenta underglow strips along the chassis sides, an amber/red-blue light bar on the roof, antenna rods, a lathe-built satellite dish dome, and a turret base mounted on the cab roof.

Now I'm adding the turret itself: a lathe-and-box gun assembly on the roof with twin forward-facing barrels and glowing muzzle tips, plus a pair of vertical exhaust stacks mounted behind the cab. I'm also laying out armor skirt panels along the chassis sides, positioning them to fit between the wheel gaps with angled cutout detailing and panel-style paint.

Now I'm computing the actual wheel coverage zones to find the clear gap for mounting the side skirts, settling on a skirt placed at roughly x=±1.3 with a neon edge accent instead of a separate fuel tank. For the rear bed, I'm designing a sealed cargo pod as a lathed octagonal capsule shape centered further back on the chassis.

Adding pod cradle supports and glowing strap bands around the hull...

I'm reworking the chassis and pod dimensions so the tail overhang lines up properly, then planning a surface decal panel on the pod flanks with a corporate "KURO-TECH" logo and hazard warning text.

I'm figuring out the lathe geometry for the pod's cross-section, testing segment counts and radii so the decal plane sits flush against the flat faces without the vertices poking through.

Then I switch to actually applying the decal onto the pod surface, placing it at a specific position and size with the direction vector pointing outward. Now I'm working through the viewer orientation math to figure out which way is "right" for the text so it reads correctly from someone standing at +X facing toward -X.

I'm also placing a rear-door decal with a locking wheel circle and hazard marking, positioning it on the flat end cap of the pod near its tapered tip, adjusting the profile points so the cap radius and decal size line up properly.

Now I'm working out the bed platform position on the chassis, matching its height against the pod's bottom clearance and setting the bed's length and center offset along the truck's z-axis. I'm also placing the cradle support wedges at a few points along the bed to hold the pod in place.

I'm reconsidering the cradle ribs as tilted boxes instead of extruded V-cutouts for simplicity, positioning three pairs at different z offsets. Since the pod should look "guarded," I'm weighing options like a roof turret, rear gunner mount, or side missile pods on the cab, leaning toward adding a turret near the pod's rear.

Now I'm adding the rear bumper with glowing red light strips, tail lights, mud flaps, a satellite dish, and side exhaust pipes, then building out the cab front grille with vent slat texture and headlight placement.

Next I'm sizing the windshield relative to the cab, building the roof light bar with glowing red/blue segments, and placing antennas with glowing tips at the back of the cab roof, then positioning the dish geometry at an angle above the cab.

Now I'm designing the turret: a hexagonal base cylinder, a boxy head, and barrel rods extending forward with small glowing muzzle tips, adjusting its z-position so it clears the windshield and roof. I'm also defining the wheel geometry with dark radial tires and hexagonal steel hubs with a bit of glow.

I'm figuring out the wheel's cyan hub disc placement on the outer face, considering adding a ring of lug bolts, and sketching tread cleats as small boxes spaced around the tire's circumference to give it texture.

Now I'm estimating total part count with 12 pieces per wheel across four wheels, then moving to fender arches as box plates sitting above the rear wheels, setting chassis and axle heights, and placing cylindrical axles running across the body—plus planning emissive seam lines along the pod.

Placing glowing strips...

Defining ring geometry...

For the pod, I'm placing an amber beacon near the top and thinking about adding a keypad panel near the rear door. I'm also positioning a second turret on the pod near z -3.3.

Now I'm planning a rear-facing turret with reversed barrel direction, and sketching out the SVG textures needed: windshield HUD gradient, side window, grille slats, a hex-logo emblem reading "KURO·VAULT / SEALED // CLASS-9" with barcode and hazard border, a rear door lock wheel with "DO NOT OPEN" text, a "CONVOY 07" cab decal, and neon signage elements.

I'm also working out the paint schemes: a countershaded dark steel-blue hull with mud wear near the bottom and scratch noise, a gunmetal pod paint with grid panel lines and grime, cab plates in a slate tone, and hazard-yellow diagonal stripes for the bumper armor.

Setting flat neon/amber/red colors and defining a box helper for parts, noting static models can skip joints and using degree-based rotations with flat shading enabled before writing the actual code.

Now I'm checking the wheel geometry's rotation and segment count to make sure the bottom-most vertices actually touch the ground plane rather than leaving a gap, since a 10-segment cylinder's vertex angles may not align cleanly after rotating the wheel into place.

Working out the rotation math so the wheel's vertex sits at the bottom with 12 segments for a clean floor contact, then positioning the tread boxes around the wheel circumference with a slight radial offset and angled rotation to follow the wheel's curve.

Settling on tire radius 0.68 with cleats just outside it, keeping the floor sink within tolerance even for the tallest part like the antenna at 4.3 units. Now I'm sketching out the cab extrusion profile and lathe helper structure for building the rest of the model.

Figuring out placement for the side window plane: positioning it on the sloped section of the cab's local z-axis, checking that the window's top edge stays below the roof curve, then converting the local coordinates into world coordinates for size and offset.

Below that I'm adding a door/logo decal plane with "CONVOY 07" text and a hex mark, positioned just under the window on the cab's lower front.

Now I'm planning the emblem SVGs: a pod decal with hazard stripes, a cyan hex logo, and transparent center so the pod's base paint shows through, plus a rear door SVG with a circular lock wheel, and considering adding a magenta glow box under the chassis.

I'm repositioning that magenta glow strip under the chassis so it clears the wheels, then adding side armor skirt panels to cover the gaps between wheels near the cab and rear, plus a mudflap past the back wheel.

Now I'm sketching a turret function that builds a hexagonal base, head box, barrels with glowing muzzles, and a glowing red sensor eye, aiming to keep the whole script around 400 lines with randomized grime detailing.

I'm deciding to skip unnecessary rng usage to avoid unused imports, planning only minimal touches like a few rivets or bolts on the bumper using a lightweight random helper, and figuring out how to attach surface decorations and stick-like strips to parts using the builder's positioning methods.

I need to guard against null hit results, give the windshield and other textured glass parts a subtle glow in their own colors, and then finalize the metadata before producing the full code output.
